correctness.rationale: For a five-vertex complement S in the squared cycle, direct cyclic-distance analysis proves that the induced k-vertex graph is disconnected exactly when S has at least two cyclic runs of length at least two. This gives exactly the facet run types (3,2) and (2,2,1). Four-faces are exactly the run types (3,1), (2,2), and (2,1,1), and every three-subset extends to one of them for k >= 3. Positive-gap compositions yield the stated counts, and substitution gives the Euler formula. A standalone exhaustive verifier independently checks connectivity, the run criterion, every face, and all formulas for 3 <= k <= 14. The finite replay is explicitly not used as the proof for arbitrary k.

originality.rationale: The primary squared-cycle paper states the W_{k+5} homotopy shape and beta formula only as Sage-supported conjectures and does not state the all-k face vector. Full-text comparison with the later three-cut squared-cycle paper shows its proved range fixes cut size three, while its higher-cut conjecture assumes n >= 2k+3. The later sequel advertises face-polynomial formulas for disjoint unions and studies squared paths and grids. Semantic database searches for the exact family, aliases, Euler formula, and A006503 connection found no covering published finding.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural exact invariant for the precise borderline squared-cycle family singled out by a published homotopy conjecture. It converts the observed beta sequence from a separate finite-range numerical conjecture into a formal Euler-characteristic consequence of the homotopy shape for every k >= 3, thereby isolating the genuinely topological part of the open problem. The result is an all-parameter structural count, not a recomputation of a small table.
